top_choice_rationale: P001 (Helpman and Melitz, B010) rewards one identifiable discovery: firm heterogeneity and selection in trade. Representative-firm trade models do not produce selection into exporting, exporter premia, entry and exit, or within-industry reallocation after liberalisation. Firm-level data in many countries have tested these predictions for over twenty years, and Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple on exporting versus foreign investment supports a two-name credit that follows the intellectual structure. Reservations remain: Bernard, Jensen, Eaton, Kortum and Hopenhayn are precursors or parallel contributors, and the size of the welfare gains is sensitive to parametric assumptions. A narrow citation on selection and reallocation, with the precursors acknowledged in the scientific background, handles these. I judge the achievement, maturity and attribution sufficient and prefer an award to no award (P000). This rests on my own recollection of the literature, not independent verification, and the convergence of colleagues on the same pair is evidence of stable attribution, not of merit.
recusal_note: No tie to Helpman or Melitz in my profile. Disclosed: my firm-dynamics and reallocation research is field-proximate to B010, and I am a frequent co-author and IIES colleague of Krusell (secretary) and Hassler (chair), both of whom support P001. Neither is a candidate. These ties are disclosed and not adjudicated.
